newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian 10-yr bonds hemmed in at 93.470.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian 10-yr bonds hemmed in at 93.470.

text.p: The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract is expected to find difficulty extending last week's strong rebound further and through 93.470 with external factors limiting the advance.
The 93.470 level, which had proved a solid support barrier before last week's steep downward break to 93.135, has now switched to resistance and formed the intra-day peak on Friday.

Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac, suggested 93.470 was a sell signal for now and he said he expected the 10-year contract to trade a more conservative range well inside 93.360 to 93.470.
The 10-year bond ended the Friday/Saturday SYCOM session at 93.420 after holding support at 93.360.

U.S. Treasuries succumbed to another volatile session on Friday against a backdrop of a falling U.S. dollar and a 247 point slump in the Dow Jones Industrial Average but had erased early steep losses by the close to finish narrowly mixed.

The fall on Wall Street, the second largest point loss on record, prompted a flight-to-quality at the short end of the U.S. Treasuries market. The long end was under pressure with the U.S. dollar which is fretting over the possibilty of tighter German monetary policy.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday is expected to keep policy on hold after the recent run of favourable inflation data.
The Reserve Bank releases its quarterly Bulletin on Tuesday, although it is expected to run on similar lines to RBA governor Ian Macfarlane's Perth speech last week.

Other events locally this week include the latest Department of Industrial Relations report on enterprise bargaining agreements. But with average weekly earnings proving benign in the second quarter the data should have modest impact.
